layers.title: Forest height
layers.description: Mean height of the forest canopy measured by NASA's GEDI laser instrument on the International Space Station, April 2019 to July 2025 (GEDI L3 Version 3). Fixed scale: 0 m is the bottom and 50 m or more is the top. Where GEDI has no measurement (mostly beyond about 52° N and S) the value comes from the NASA SVS 4950 visualization instead; the two are never blended. Taller forest sounds as a higher, fuller note. This is the fixed base layer.

source.title: GEDI L3 Gridded Land Surface Metrics V3 (NASA GEDI, ORNL DAAC), filled with NASA SVS 4950

layers.title: Wildfire smoke
layers.description: Fine particles (PM2.5) in the air near the ground, mostly smoke from fires, modelled hour by hour by NASA's GEOS-CF system for 1 to 7 September 2026, in the fire season; one turn of the planet is one day. Fixed scale: 0 µg/m³ is the bottom and 150 µg/m³ or more is the top. More smoke makes the sound rougher and darker.

layers.title: Atmospheric CO2
layers.description: Carbon dioxide moving through the atmosphere from NASA's DYAMOND simulation with the GEOS model. Over the Americas and the Atlantic it moves from 23 to 25 February 2020, hour by hour; the rest of the planet is a fixed picture with each region on the date of the view that covers it, between 14 January and 3 March 2020 (where two views overlap their dates are blended). It is the global context, not a measured effect of the Amazon. More CO2 makes the breathing pulse faster and heavier.

layers.title: Lightning
layers.description: Where lightning was seen from the International Space Station (NASA's LIS instrument), month by month from January 2017 to July 2023. Each frame shows only its own month, nothing accumulated, so the storm belt moves north and south with the seasons. Brighter means lightning in more of the ten-day windows of that month; it is a relative frequency read from a NASA visualization, not a flash count. LIS sees only between about 55° N and 55° S.

source.title: Lightning Events Detected from the ISS 2017-2023 (NASA SVS 5011)
